claim_text: Maintain proper posture while sitting to prevent back pain.

adjudication.reason: The reviewed evidence does not establish support or refutation under this policy.
adjudication.summary: The two appraised abstracts concern treatment in people already experiencing low back pain and mixed review-level evidence about physical exposure and causality. They do not establish that an isolated, defined proper sitting posture prevents back-pain onset or recurrence. This bounded assisted assessment does not establish that posture is irrelevant or ineffective.

criteria.wording: Maintain proper posture while sitting to prevent back pain.
criteria.rationale: The randomized trial enrolled 60 patients with existing nonspecific low back pain. Both arms performed core stability exercise; the multidimensional arm also received pain-principles and management training. Improved pain, disability and measured posture after this combined treatment do not isolate a preventive effect of sitting posture. The umbrella review includes 41 reviews and reports mixed temporal and dose-response evidence and no causal consensus. Association and lack of causal consensus neither prove posture-caused pain nor prove no posture effect. Proper posture is not operationalized in the claim, and prevention must be distinguished from treating current symptoms.

citations.quote: The purpose of this study was to investigate the effects of multidimensional approach model on the pain, disability, and sitting posture in patients with nonspecific low back pain (LBP).
Evidence that these factors precede first time LBP or have a dose response relationship with LBP outcomes was mixed.

evidence_gaps: Define the proposed sitting posture and intended prevention population, including whether onset or recurrence is the target.
An isolated sitting-posture intervention with incident or recurrent back-pain outcomes is not established by the appraised trial abstract.
Confounding, mixed interventions, review overlap, risk of bias, effect sizes and clinical importance require further appraisal.
Assisted appraisal of 2/77 candidate abstracts. Other candidates were not appraised in this assessment. No full-text, exhaustive-search or systematic risk-of-bias appraisal was performed.

review.reviewer: ChatGPT-assisted abstract assessment and critical recheck

adjudication.decision_scope: Rule-based synthesis of supplied reviewed assessments; citation presence does not prove entailment or scientific correctness.
